page: Amazon Web Services h1.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features 32 virtual CPUs powered by 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 8,000 GB of direct-attached local HDD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, alongside a 45 MB L3 CPU cache.

In synthetic benchmark evaluations, the h1.8xlarge demonstrates average multi-core CPU capabilities alongside poor single-core execution speed. Single-threaded stress-ng tests achieved a score of 864.69, while multi-core stress-ng reached 16279.61. The system recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 889.0 and a multi-core score of 7383.0. Memory bandwidth testing yielded 1238.3 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 52.11 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read operations, though uncached write operations showed weaker performance at 24.24 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measured 19.97 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 15.46 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds were restricted by the legacy CPU architecture, yielding 802.38 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model for prompt processing and 4.78 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

By pairing a balanced compute-to-memory footprint with high-capacity local magnetic storage, the h1.8xlarge offers cost-effective resource density for sequential data access patterns. The reliance on HDD storage makes this instance less suited for low-latency random IOPS requirements typical of relational databases. Instead, it offers high value for batch processing pipelines, log analytics platforms, data lakes, distributed file systems, and bulk storage environments where storage volume and sequential read throughput are prioritized over absolute CPU speed.
description: Amazon Web Services h1.8xlarge is a storage-optimized server configuration designed for data-intensive processing tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 128 GB of memory. The instance features 8,000 GB of direct-attached local HDD storage and 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth on the Xen hypervisor. Performance evaluations reveal solid multi-core compute capabilities, such as a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 16279.61 and 19.97 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-threaded performance remains lower. With its large local storage capacity and balanced memory profile, the h1.8xlarge provides economical resource density for bulk data processing, log analytics, distributed file systems, and batch data lake workloads that benefit from high sequential storage access rather than high random IOPS performance.
